<reason>Both sides built strong, well-grounded cases, but CON controlled the decisive clash. PRO's early concession that programs "launch near-universal and tighten later" handed CON a live contradiction: the informal fisherman/driver is covered only while the program is near-universal and is "released" the moment it becomes genuinely targeted — a tension PRO never resolved, only restated. Worse, PRO admitted "compensation before the shock was never on the menu," which CON crystallized into the voting issue: under the motion, the price shock is certain and day-one, while the compensation is contingent on registries, budgets, and future "tightening." PRO's main counter — that price controls inevitably "detonate" into uncompensated shocks — was effectively blunted by CON's reframe: Nigeria and Iran are evidence about what removal does, and those governments were executing exactly what the motion prescribes, not watching subsidies collapse on their own. CON's Q1 pressure on asymmetric realism was answered cleanly by CON itself in Rebuttal 2 with the removal-versus-collapse distinction, while PRO's A2 answer ("never on the menu") became a concession. PRO's categorical-criteria rescue (rural households, fuel-intensive occupations) was a genuinely good move and kept the debate close, and PRO's failure-mode comparison was vivid, but the sequencing burden was never squarely discharged. CON also loses a small execution cost on a clipped opening; PRO lost two clipped turns, compounding the sense that its strongest extensions arrived truncated. Slight edge to B on grounding: its Nigeria/Iran mechanism detail was plausible without fake precision. Clear but competitive win for the opposition.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B4.1–B4.6: CON's Rebuttal 2 reattributed every "detonation" example to removal rather than subsidy failure, then weaponized PRO's own A1 ("phase out as capacity improves") against PRO's A2 (categorical criteria catch the fisherman), showing the fisherman is caught only while near-universal and dropped once targeting tightens — the sharpest, most damaging exchange of the debate.</best_rebuttal>
